subject: Shiny-Server error, says "The application failed to start"

messages.author: 14133ab7424f3afd
messages.subject: Shiny-Server error, says "The application failed to start"
parts:
Hi, 

The local version Shiny worked great on my laptop, then I tried to deploy the same codes to my linux workstation.
Carefully follow instructions on this page: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server
Finally, enter "shiny-server" in the terminal (sudo shiny-server doesn't work, says "sudo: shiny-server: command not found"), it outputs:
[2013-04-11 23:02:58.623] [INFO] shiny-server - Shiny Server v0.3.5 (Node.js v0.10.4)
[2013-04-11 23:02:58.626] [INFO] shiny-server - Using config file "/etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf"
[2013-04-11 23:02:58.663] [INFO] shiny-server - Starting listener on 0.0.0.0:3838

Then, from the browser, I typed in "http://<linux-hostname>:3838/HelloWorld/", the expected UI didn't show up, instead:

An error has occurred

The application failed to start.

EACCES, open '/var/shiny-server/log/HelloWorld-chance-20130411-230413-45596.log'


Then I tried "http://<linux-hostname>:3838/", it did show the index:

Index of /

  • HelloWorld/

Does that mean the shiny-server itself is running well? Since if I stop the shiny-server from the terminal, both the above links don't work (shows nothing, 404 like page).

Then probably something wrong with node.js?
I followed steps here https://github.com/joyent/node/wiki/Installation (My OS is RHEL)
After installation finished, I did a "make test", it did show one error:
=== release test-net-connect-unref ===                                         
Path: simple/test-net-connect-unref
events.js:72
        throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
              ^
Error: connect ECONNREFUSED
    at errnoException (net.js:883:11)
    at Object.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (net.js:874:19)

Any thoughts?

Thanks,
Chance

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny-Server error, says "The application failed to start"
parts:
Oh, didn't see your note about not using sudo--that's the problem.

Some Linux distros don't put /usr/local/bin in sudo's $PATH. You might be able to work around it by doing this instead:

su - -c shiny-server

messages.subject: Re: Shiny-Server error, says "The application failed to start"
parts:
Thank you so much, Joe! sudo is the cause!

Since I am not the root, so su - -c shiny-server doesn't work (which asks for the root password)
What I did is:
sudo su
then: add /usr/local/bin to $PATH
then: shiny-server
then: Boom, the "shiny" server!

Thanks again:)
